QUIC TLS handshake setup, processing, callbacks, and handshake data management.

# Purpose
This file implements the QUIC and TLS integration layer for `fd_quic`. It creates and manages an embedded `fd_tls_t` instance inside `fd_quic_tls_t`, sets up the TLS signer, random source, key exchange material, mock X.509 certificate, and ALPN value, and connects TLS callbacks back into the QUIC code. The main entry points are [`fd_quic_tls_new`](<#fd_quic_tls_new>), [`fd_quic_tls_delete`](<#fd_quic_tls_delete>), [`fd_quic_tls_hs_new`](<#fd_quic_tls_hs_new>), [`fd_quic_tls_hs_delete`](<#fd_quic_tls_hs_delete>), and [`fd_quic_tls_process`](<#fd_quic_tls_process>), which together create a handshake object, start a client or server handshake, process received handshake records, and report completion or failure.

The file also defines the callback functions that `fd_tls` uses to exchange data with QUIC. [`fd_quic_tls_sendmsg`](<#fd_quic_tls_sendmsg>) stores outgoing handshake records in per-encryption-level queues, [`fd_quic_tls_secrets`](<#fd_quic_tls_secrets>) forwards new read and write secrets to the QUIC layer, [`fd_quic_tls_rand`](<#fd_quic_tls_rand>) supplies random bytes, and [`fd_quic_tls_tp_self`](<#fd_quic_tls_tp_self>) and [`fd_quic_tls_tp_peer`](<#fd_quic_tls_tp_peer>) handle QUIC transport parameter encoding and delivery. Helper functions such as [`fd_quic_tls_get_hs_data`](<#fd_quic_tls_get_hs_data>), [`fd_quic_tls_get_next_hs_data`](<#fd_quic_tls_get_next_hs_data>), [`fd_quic_tls_pop_hs_data`](<#fd_quic_tls_pop_hs_data>), and [`fd_quic_tls_clear_hs_data`](<#fd_quic_tls_clear_hs_data>) provide access to the queued handshake data that QUIC must send to the peer.
